# `\` — Scan

`f\Y` scans the last axis from left to right. Each result combines the previous result, as `f`'s left argument, with the next item: `-\1 2 3` is `1`, `1-2` and `(1-2)-3`.

```bpl
+\1 2 3            ⍝ 1 3 6
-\1 2 3            ⍝ 1 ¯1 ¯4
```

`S f\ Y` starts from seed `S` as the first previous result, and leaves the seed out of the result.

```bpl
10-\1 2 3          ⍝ 9 7 4
100+\10 20         ⍝ 110 130
```

Each lane starts from the whole seed. Use Rank for separate seeds per cell.

```bpl
M←[1 2 3 ⋄ 4 5 6]
10 20+\⍤0 1 M      ⍝ [11 13 16 ⋄ 24 29 35]
[10]+\1 2 3        ⍝ [[11] [13] [16]]
```

Empty scans and unseeded singletons make no calls. [Axis](axis.qmd) `⍠K` selects the axis, and [`⍀`](backslash-bar.qmd) defaults to the first.

```bpl
+\⍠0 [1 2 3 ⋄ 4 5 6]  ⍝ [1 2 3 ⋄ 5 7 9]
```

APL difference: every scan left-accumulates, including dfns.

## Errors

- `DOMAIN`: a subject operand. Expand with [`#⁻¹`](hash.qmd#expand)
